page_title: Generalized Neural Operator for Parametric and Boundary-Value Problems
subject: Generalized Neural Operator
statement: The paper proposes Generalized Neural Operator, which formalizes classical conditions for well-posedness within neural operators.

page_title: Generalized Neural Operator for Parametric and Boundary-Value Problems
subject: Generalized Neural Operator
statement: Generalized Neural Operator introduces a parameter-gated mixture of kernels for efficient parameter generalization and a generalized boundary transfer operator that projects arbitrary boundary constraints into a unified latent Dirichlet representation.

page_title: Generalized Neural Operator for Parametric and Boundary-Value Problems
subject: Generalized Neural Operator
statement: The paper demonstrates that Generalized Neural Operator achieves superior generalization across heterogeneous physical regimes while maintaining strict inference efficiency comparable to conventional numerical baselines.

page_title: Efficient Online LLM Watermark Detection via Rao-Blackwellized E-Processes
subject: Rao-Blackwellized e-processes
statement: The paper develops an efficient online watermark detection framework with anytime-valid inference based on Rao-Blackwellized e-processes, enabling recursive token-level evidence updates without storing the full history.

page_title: Efficient Online LLM Watermark Detection via Rao-Blackwellized E-Processes
subject: Rao-Blackwellized e-processes
statement: The paper instantiates the framework for Gumbel-max watermark and reduces token-level dependence testing to a pivot-induced sequential testing problem with explicit null distribution.

page_title: Efficient Online LLM Watermark Detection via Rao-Blackwellized E-Processes
subject: Rao-Blackwellized e-processes
statement: The paper proves anytime-valid Type I error control under arbitrary optional stopping and establishes positive asymptotic log-growth under watermarking, implying consistency of the proposed stopping rules.

page_title: On Improving Faithfulness of Podcasts from Documents
subject: catch-n-repair
statement: The paper proposes catch-n-repair, a model-agnostic framework that detects and rewrites unfaithful conversational turns while preserving conversational flow.

page_title: On Improving Faithfulness of Podcasts from Documents
subject: catch-n-repair
statement: Experiments demonstrate that catch-n-repair achieves consistent improvements in faithfulness across both in-domain and out-of-domain settings.

page_title: On the Convergence of Stochastic Low-Rank Adaptation
subject: LoRA-NSGDM
statement: The paper proposes LoRA-NSGDM, which finds an ε-stationary point with O(ε^-8) stochastic oracle complexity under unbiased gradient estimates and finite variance.

page_title: On the Convergence of Stochastic Low-Rank Adaptation
subject: LoRA-STORM
statement: The paper proposes LoRA-STORM using variance reduction strategy, which improves stochastic oracle complexity to O(ε^-6) under mean-square smoothness condition.

page_title: Unified Static-Dynamic Pruning for Efficient LLM Inference
subject: SPDP
statement: The paper presents SPDP, a unified sparse-inference framework that integrates unstructured static pruning with input-adaptive dynamic pruning for efficient LLM inference on GPUs.

page_title: Unified Static-Dynamic Pruning for Efficient LLM Inference
subject: SPDP
statement: The paper reports that SPDP achieves 1.24x-1.37x average speedup (up to 2.51x) over state-of-the-art sparse frameworks such as SpInfer.

page_title: Unified Static-Dynamic Pruning for Efficient LLM Inference
subject: SPDP
statement: SPDP matches perplexity with up to 25% higher sparsity compared to existing sparse inference methods.

page_title: Zero-Shot Mission-Level Evaluation for Aerial MLLM Agents
subject: MissionBench
statement: The paper introduces MissionBench, a benchmark for mission-level evaluation of multimodal large language models in aerial 3D environments.

page_title: Zero-Shot Mission-Level Evaluation for Aerial MLLM Agents
subject: MissionBench
statement: MissionBench comprises 120 missions across five simulated 3D environments and four task families for autonomous embodied reasoning.

page_title: Zero-Shot Mission-Level Evaluation for Aerial MLLM Agents
subject: MissionBench
statement: Across 22 open- and closed-source MLLMs evaluated on MissionBench, the strongest model succeeds on fewer than 35% of missions compared to 84.4% human performance.

page_title: Rethinking Multi-Branch and Cross-Backbone Fusion for Vehicle Re-Identification in the Foundation-Model Era
subject: DINOv3-ConvNeXt
statement: The paper shows that a single DINOv3-pretrained ConvNeXt trained with a tuned recipe achieves 88.19 mAP on VeRi-Wild Small and 77.47 mAP on VeRi-Wild Large.

page_title: Rethinking Multi-Branch and Cross-Backbone Fusion for Vehicle Re-Identification in the Foundation-Model Era
subject: DINOv3-ConvNeXt
statement: The paper demonstrates that improving a single strong foundation-model backbone together with retrieval-stage re-ranking is more effective than increasing architectural complexity through additional branches.

page_title: A Leakage-Free Stacked Ensemble Method for Multiclass Classification
subject: LFS-FRAME
statement: The paper proposes LFS-FRAME, a Leakage-Free Stacked ensemble framework that integrates functional learning using Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KAN) and rule-based learning via XGBoost.

page_title: A Leakage-Free Stacked Ensemble Method for Multiclass Classification
subject: LFS-FRAME
statement: LFS-FRAME reports overall accuracy of 89.85% in identifying major families and 81.74% in identifying sub-families.

page_title: MemNMF: Memory-Augmented NMF on LPC Spectra for Anomalous Sound Detection
subject: MemNMF
statement: The paper proposes MemNMF, a constrained reconstruction method that operates on Linear Predictive Coding spectrum for anomalous sound detection.

page_title: MemNMF: Memory-Augmented NMF on LPC Spectra for Anomalous Sound Detection
subject: MemNMF
statement: MemNMF yields gains on MIMII and DCASE 2020 Task 2 with especially strong robustness under noisy, non-stationary settings.

page_title: Reasoning Denoiser: Denoising Reasoning Traces for Hallucination Detection in Large Reasoning Models
subject: REDE
statement: The paper proposes REDE, a novel learning framework for denoising reasoning traces for hallucination detection in large reasoning models.

page_title: Reasoning Denoiser: Denoising Reasoning Traces for Hallucination Detection in Large Reasoning Models
subject: REDE
statement: REDE leverages final-answer attention as an automatic supervision signal to shape the step-level representation space for identifying noisy steps.

page_title: Reasoning Denoiser: Denoising Reasoning Traces for Hallucination Detection in Large Reasoning Models
subject: REDE
statement: Extensive experiments on multiple reasoning benchmarks show that REDE consistently improves detection performance over competitive baselines.

page_title: Benchmarking Text-to-SQL under Role-Based Access Control
subject: Text-to-SQL-RBAC
statement: The paper presents a comprehensive text-to-SQL benchmarking framework with realistic role-based access control (RBAC) constraints.

page_title: Benchmarking Text-to-SQL under Role-Based Access Control
subject: Text-to-SQL-RBAC
statement: The paper shows that many text-to-SQL solutions with high benchmarking scores under unrestricted settings suffer sharp performance degradation once access constraints are in place.

page_title: Bowel Obstruction Detection and Localization on Abdominal CT with Deep Learning
subject: Multi-task obstruction detector
statement: The paper proposes a deep learning framework with a multi-task objective that jointly detects bowel obstruction and localizes its transition zone.

page_title: Bowel Obstruction Detection and Localization on Abdominal CT with Deep Learning
subject: Multi-task obstruction detector
statement: The model achieves obstruction detection test accuracy of 93% and Hit@10 transition zone localization of 95%.

page_title: Industrial Tokenization for LLM-Based Health Intelligence: A Federated Architecture for Industrial Evidence Integration
subject: Industrial Tokenization
statement: The paper introduces Industrial Tokenization, a conceptual interface for transforming source-specific analytical outputs into structured Industrial Tokens.

page_title: Industrial Tokenization for LLM-Based Health Intelligence: A Federated Architecture for Industrial Evidence Integration
subject: Industrial Tokenization
statement: A federated industrial architecture is proposed where heterogeneous analytical subsystems retain autonomy while exposing standardized Industrial Tokens.

page_title: Trajectory-Regularized Stochastic Optimal Control via KL Divergence
subject: TRSOC
statement: The paper introduces TRSOC, which augments stochastic optimal control with Kullback-Leibler divergence between controlled and reference trajectory distributions.

page_title: Trajectory-Regularized Stochastic Optimal Control via KL Divergence
subject: TRSOC
statement: In the linear-quadratic (LQ) setting, TRSOC admits a closed-form solution with an augmented control cost.

page_title: Why Large Language Models and Humans Converge and Diverge in Evaluating Creativity
subject: LLM creativity evaluators
statement: The paper shows that LLMs generally relied on a narrower subset of human creativity evaluation standards.

page_title: Why Large Language Models and Humans Converge and Diverge in Evaluating Creativity
subject: LLM creativity evaluators
object: converge on novelty, diverge on context
statement: The study finds that convergence with human standards was strongest in the novelty dimension, whereas divergence was clearest in the contextual dimension.

page_title: Why Large Language Models and Humans Converge and Diverge in Evaluating Creativity
subject: LLM creativity evaluators
statement: LLMs were less sensitive to contextual information: such information significantly altered human creativity ratings but left LLM ratings largely unchanged.

page_title: Convergence analysis of a family of Zermelo-type iterations for the Bradley--Terry model
subject: Zermelo-type iterations
statement: The paper shows that for synchronous updates, the algorithm may fail to converge when α<1.

page_title: Convergence analysis of a family of Zermelo-type iterations for the Bradley--Terry model
subject: Zermelo-type iterations
statement: For asynchronous updates, the paper establishes that α=0 is optimal under the Bradley-Terry model, as local convergence factor is provably monotonically increasing in α.

page_title: Optimization of time-consuming experimental conditions using pseudo-experimental data guided by adaptive polynomial regression
subject: PolyBO
statement: The paper develops PolyBO to improve optimization time by generating high-quality pseudo-experimental data with adaptively updated polynomial regression.

page_title: Optimization of time-consuming experimental conditions using pseudo-experimental data guided by adaptive polynomial regression
subject: PolyBO
statement: PolyBO reduced optimization time by a median of 42% on synthetic benchmark functions with diverse landscapes.

page_title: Optimization of time-consuming experimental conditions using pseudo-experimental data guided by adaptive polynomial regression
subject: PolyBO
statement: For a real-world material composition optimization problem, PolyBO reduced optimization time by a median of 96% compared with conventional methods.

page_title: IFCLoRA: Topology-Aware Rank Allocation for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning
subject: IFCLoRA
statement: The paper proposes IFCLoRA, a topology-aware rank allocation method for LoRA applied before fine-tuning.

page_title: IFCLoRA: Topology-Aware Rank Allocation for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning
subject: IFCLoRA
statement: IFCLoRA computes Information-Flow Centrality scores by combining global information-flow topology priors with local gradient sensitivity.

page_title: IFCLoRA: Topology-Aware Rank Allocation for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning
subject: IFCLoRA
statement: On mathematical reasoning with LLaMA 3 8B, IFCLoRA improves over standard LoRA by 1.36 percent at rank 4 and 1.82 percent at rank 8.

page_title: Class-Balanced Softmax: A Bayes Theory-Based Method for Long-Tailed Recognition
subject: Class-Balanced Softmax
statement: The paper proposes Class-Balanced Softmax (CBS), a simple logit adjustment rooted in a theoretical Bayesian framework for long-tailed recognition.

page_title: Class-Balanced Softmax: A Bayes Theory-Based Method for Long-Tailed Recognition
subject: Class-Balanced Softmax
statement: The paper characterizes the preference issue, wherein models exhibit higher training error for classes with limited data, and demonstrates that CBS effectively mitigates this issue.

page_title: Class-Balanced Softmax: A Bayes Theory-Based Method for Long-Tailed Recognition
subject: Class-Balanced Softmax
statement: Extensive experiments on large-scale benchmarks show that CBS is highly scalable and outperforms existing methods, including Balanced Softmax.

page_title: General Value Functions for Remaining Useful Life and Failure-Mode Prediction
subject: Vector GVF with TD estimation
statement: The paper formulates prognostics as vector General Value Function (GVF) prediction on an absorbing degradation process, estimating RUL with temporal-difference estimator TD(n,λ).

page_title: General Value Functions for Remaining Useful Life and Failure-Mode Prediction
subject: Vector GVF with TD estimation
statement: The paper shows that TD improves RUL and failure-mode prediction relative to supervised Monte Carlo control, especially under scarce complete labels.
